commands.name: ABS
commands.description: The absolute value of x: x without its sign; the length of a complex number.

commands.name: ACOS
commands.description: The arc cosine of x, in the current angle mode.

commands.name: ACOSH
commands.description: The inverse hyperbolic cosine of x.

commands.name: ADV
commands.description: Feeds the printer paper by one line.

commands.name: AGRAPH
commands.description: Draws the Alpha register as dot columns on the display: each character is one column of eight dots, placed at the row in y and the column in x.

commands.name: AIP
commands.description: Appends x's integer part to the Alpha register.

commands.name: ALENG
commands.description: How many characters the Alpha register holds.

commands.name: ALL
commands.description: Shows numbers with all their digits (ALL display format).

commands.name: ALLΣ
commands.description: Statistics with all 13 summation registers, which every curve fit needs.

commands.name: ALPHA
commands.description: Opens the ALPHA menu, for typing letters into the Alpha register or a name.

commands.name: AND
commands.description: The bitwise AND of y and x, as 36-bit integers.

commands.name: AOFF
commands.description: Leaves Alpha mode.

commands.name: AON
commands.description: Turns Alpha mode on, showing the Alpha register with the ALPHA menu.

commands.name: ARCL
commands.description: Appends a register's or variable's contents to the Alpha register; numbers in the current display format. Its key in Alpha mode is RCL.

commands.name: AROT
commands.description: Rotates the Alpha register by x characters, to the left for positive x.

commands.name: ASHF
commands.description: Drops the six leftmost characters of the Alpha register.

commands.name: ASIN
commands.description: The arc sine of x, in the current angle mode.

commands.name: ASINH
commands.description: The inverse hyperbolic sine of x.

commands.name: ASSIGN
commands.description: Puts a function, a program or a variable on a key of the CUSTOM menu.

commands.name: ASTO
commands.description: Stores the Alpha register's first six characters in a register or variable. Its key in Alpha mode is STO.

commands.name: ATAN
commands.description: The arc tangent of x, in the current angle mode.

commands.name: ATANH
commands.description: The inverse hyperbolic tangent of x.

commands.name: ATOX
commands.description: Removes the leftmost character of the Alpha register and returns its character code.

commands.name: AVIEW
commands.description: Shows the Alpha register on the display.

commands.name: BASE
commands.description: Opens the BASE menu: hexadecimal, decimal, octal and binary integers and their logic.

commands.name: BASE+
commands.description: Adds y and x as 36-bit integers. The + key in the BASE menu.

commands.name: BASE-
commands.description: Subtracts x from y as 36-bit integers. The − key in the BASE menu.

commands.name: BASE×
commands.description: Multiplies y by x as 36-bit integers. The × key in the BASE menu.

commands.name: BASE÷
commands.description: Divides y by x as 36-bit integers, dropping the remainder. The ÷ key in the BASE menu.

commands.name: BASE+/-
commands.description: Changes the sign of x as a 36-bit two's complement integer. The +/- key in the BASE menu.

commands.name: BEEP
commands.description: Plays a short tune of four tones.

commands.name: BEST
commands.description: Picks the curve-fit model that fits the statistics data best.

commands.name: BINM
commands.description: Binary mode: shows integers in base 2.

commands.name: BIT?
commands.description: Tests bit x of y. A program runs its next line only if the bit is set.

commands.name: BST
commands.description: Moves the program pointer back one line. With no menu shown, the ▲ key does it.

commands.name: CATALOG
commands.description: Opens the CATALOG menu: functions, programs, and the real, complex and matrix variables.

commands.name: CF
commands.description: Clears a flag.

commands.name: CLA
commands.description: Clears the Alpha register.

commands.name: CLALL
commands.description: Clears all programs and data, after asking. It cannot be undone.

commands.name: CLD
commands.description: Removes the message shown on the display.

commands.name: CLEAR
commands.description: Opens the CLEAR menu.

commands.name: CLKEYS
commands.description: Removes every assignment from the CUSTOM menu.

commands.name: CLLCD
commands.description: Blanks the whole display.

commands.name: CLMENU
commands.description: Removes every key definition of the programmable menu.

commands.name: CLP
commands.description: Deletes a program from memory.

commands.name: CLRG
commands.description: Sets every numbered storage register to zero.

commands.name: CLST
commands.description: Sets all four stack registers (X to T) to zero.

commands.name: CLV
commands.description: Deletes a variable from memory.

commands.name: CLX
commands.description: Sets x to zero. The ⬅ key does it too when no number is being typed.

commands.name: CLΣ
commands.description: Clears the statistics data in the summation registers.

commands.name: COMB
commands.description: The number of ways to choose x items from y, ignoring order.

commands.name: COMPLEX
commands.description: Joins y and x into the complex number y + ix, or splits a complex x into its two parts (also for matrices).
commands.stack: y x → y+ix; z → re im

commands.name: CONVERT
commands.description: Opens the CONVERT menu: angle and time conversions, polar and rectangular coordinates, number parts.

commands.name: CORR
commands.description: The correlation coefficient of the statistics data for the current curve-fit model.

commands.name: COS
commands.description: The cosine of x, in the current angle mode.

commands.name: COSH
commands.description: The hyperbolic cosine of x.

commands.name: CPXRES
commands.description: Lets functions return complex results from real arguments (the square root of −1 gives i).

commands.name: CPX?
commands.description: Tests whether x is a complex number. A program runs its next line only if so.

commands.name: CROSS
commands.description: Cross product of y and x, two vectors (matrices or complex numbers).

commands.name: CUSTOM
commands.description: Opens the CUSTOM menu, the keys you assigned.

commands.name: DECM
commands.description: Decimal mode for the BASE menu: shows integers in base 10.

commands.name: DEG
commands.description: Degrees angle mode.

commands.name: DEL
commands.description: Deletes a number of lines from the current program, in program entry.

commands.name: DELAY
commands.description: Sets the printer's delay after each line to x seconds.

commands.name: DELR
commands.description: Deletes the current row of the matrix open in the editor or indexed.

commands.name: DET
commands.description: The determinant of the square matrix in x.

commands.name: DIM
commands.description: Makes a named matrix y rows by x columns, creating it if needed.

commands.name: DIM?
commands.description: How many rows and columns the matrix in x has.

commands.name: DISP
commands.description: Opens the DISP menu: display formats and the radix mark.

commands.name: DOT
commands.description: Dot product of y and x, two vectors (matrices or complex numbers).

commands.name: DSE
commands.long: Decrement, skip if less or equal
commands.description: Takes the step from a loop counter ccccccc.fffii in a register or variable; in a program the next line is skipped once the counter is at or below fff.

commands.name: E
commands.description: Starts the exponent of the number being typed: 3 E 4 is 3×10⁴.

commands.name: EDIT
commands.description: Opens the matrix in x in the matrix editor.

commands.name: EDITN
commands.description: Opens a named matrix in the matrix editor.

commands.name: END
commands.description: Ends a program. Every program ends with one.

commands.name: ENG
commands.description: Engineering notation with a number of digits: exponents in multiples of three.

commands.name: ENTER
commands.description: Ends number entry and copies x into y; the stack lifts and t is lost.

commands.name: EXIT
commands.description: Leaves the current menu, or stops what is being typed or prompted.

commands.name: EXITALL
commands.description: Leaves all menus.

commands.name: EXPF
commands.description: Exponential curve-fit model: y = b·e^(m·x).

commands.name: E↑X
commands.description: The natural exponential: e to the power x.

commands.name: E↑X-1
commands.description: eˣ − 1, accurate for x close to zero.

commands.name: FC?
commands.description: Tests whether a flag is clear. A program runs its next line only if so.

commands.name: FC?C
commands.description: Tests whether a flag is clear, then clears it. In a program, the next line runs only if it was clear. Flags 00-35 and 81-99 only.

commands.name: FCSTX
commands.description: The x value the current curve fit gives for the y in x.

commands.name: FCSTY
commands.description: The y value the current curve fit gives for the x in x.

commands.name: FIX
commands.description: Fixed notation with a number of digits after the point.

commands.name: FLAGS
commands.description: Opens the FLAGS menu: setting, clearing and testing flags.

commands.name: FNRM
commands.description: Frobenius norm of x, a matrix: the square root of all its elements squared and added up.

commands.name: FP
commands.description: The fractional part of x.

commands.name: FS?
commands.description: Tests whether a flag is set. A program runs its next line only if so.

commands.name: FS?C
commands.description: Tests a flag and clears it afterwards. In a program, the next line runs only if the flag was set. Flags 00-35 and 81-99 only.

commands.name: GAMMA
commands.description: The gamma function of x; for a positive integer n, Γ(n) is (n−1)!.

commands.name: GETKEY
commands.description: Waits for a key and returns its number: 1-37 for the keys, 38-74 for the shifted ones.

commands.name: GETM
commands.description: Copies a part of the indexed matrix, y rows by x columns from the current element, into x.

commands.name: GRAD
commands.description: Grads angle mode (400 to the circle).

commands.name: GROW
commands.description: Grow mode for the matrix editor: moving past the last element adds a row.

commands.name: GTO
commands.description: Goes to a label: from the keyboard it moves the program pointer, in a program it branches.

commands.name: GTO .
commands.description: Goes to a line number or a global label in program memory, without running anything. Not programmable.

commands.name: GTO ..
commands.description: Goes to a new, empty program space after the last program, ready for a new one. Not programmable.

commands.name: HEXM
commands.description: Hexadecimal mode: shows integers in base 16.

commands.name: HMS+
commands.description: Adds y and x, both in hours-minutes-seconds form (H.MMSSss).

commands.name: HMS-
commands.description: Subtracts x from y, both in hours-minutes-seconds form (H.MMSSss).

commands.name: I+
commands.description: Moves the row pointer of the indexed matrix down one row.

commands.name: I-
commands.description: Moves the row pointer of the indexed matrix up one row.

commands.name: INDEX
commands.description: Makes a named matrix the indexed matrix, for the element and row functions.

commands.name: INPUT
commands.description: In a program: shows a register or variable with its value and stops, so you can change it; R/S stores x and goes on.

commands.name: INSR
commands.description: Inserts a row into the indexed matrix.

commands.name: INTEG
commands.description: Integrates the chosen program with respect to a variable.

commands.name: INVRT
commands.description: The inverse of the square matrix in x.

commands.name: IP
commands.description: The integer part of x.

commands.name: ISG
commands.description: Adds the step to a loop counter ccccccc.fffii in a register or variable; in a program the next line is skipped once the counter is above fff.

commands.name: J+
commands.description: Moves the column pointer of the indexed matrix right one column.

commands.name: J-
commands.description: Moves the column pointer of the indexed matrix left one column.

commands.name: KEYASN
commands.description: CUSTOM menu shows your key assignments (the other choice is LCLBL).

commands.name: KEYG
commands.description: In a program: makes a menu key branch to a label (for the programmable menu).

commands.name: KEYX
commands.description: In a program: makes a menu key run a label as a subroutine (for the programmable menu).

commands.name: LASTX
commands.description: Recalls the x a function last used.

commands.name: LBL
commands.description: Puts a label in a program, for running it and branching to it.

commands.name: LCLBL
commands.description: CUSTOM menu shows the local labels A-J and a-e of the current program.

commands.name: LINF
commands.description: Linear curve-fit model: y = m·x + b.

commands.name: LINΣ
commands.description: Statistics with the six summation registers of a linear fit only.

commands.name: LIST
commands.description: Prints a number of lines of the current program. Not programmable.

commands.name: LN
commands.description: The natural logarithm of x.

commands.name: LN1+X
commands.description: ln(1 + x), accurate for x close to zero.

commands.name: LOG
commands.description: Base-10 logarithm of x.

commands.name: LOGF
commands.description: Logarithmic curve-fit model: y = b + m·ln x.

commands.name: MAN
commands.description: Manual print mode: the printer prints only what you ask for.

commands.name: MAT?
commands.description: Tests whether x is a matrix. A program runs its next line only if so.

commands.name: MATRIX
commands.description: Opens the MATRIX menu.

commands.name: MEAN
commands.description: The means of the x values and of the y values of the statistics data.

commands.name: MENU
commands.description: In a program: shows the programmable menu, whose keys KEYG and KEYX define.

commands.name: MOD
commands.description: The remainder of y divided by x.

commands.name: MODES
commands.description: Opens the MODES menu: angle and coordinate modes, complex results, register count, beeper.

commands.name: MVAR
commands.description: In a program: declares a variable for the Solver's or the integrator's variable menu.

commands.name: N!
commands.description: The factorial of x.

commands.name: NEWMAT
commands.description: Creates a matrix of y rows and x columns, all zeros.

commands.name: NORM
commands.description: Normal print mode: the printer records the keys you press.

commands.name: NOT
commands.description: The bitwise NOT of x, as a 36-bit integer.

commands.name: OCTM
commands.description: Octal mode: shows integers in base 8.

commands.name: OFF
commands.description: Turns the calculator off. The shifted key does it from the keyboard; XEQ "OFF" is the form a program uses.

commands.name: OLD
commands.description: Recalls the current element of the indexed matrix (as RCLEL does).

commands.name: ON
commands.description: Keeps the calculator on: it no longer turns itself off after ten minutes.

commands.name: OR
commands.description: The bitwise OR of y and x, as 36-bit integers.

commands.name: PERM
commands.description: The number of ordered arrangements of x items taken from y.

commands.name: PGM.FCN
commands.description: Opens the PGM.FCN menu: programming functions.

commands.name: PGMINT
commands.description: Chooses the program to integrate.

commands.name: PGMSLV
commands.description: Chooses the program to solve.

commands.name: PIXEL
commands.description: Turns on the display dot at row y and column x.

commands.name: POLAR
commands.description: Polar coordinate mode: complex numbers show as a length and an angle.

commands.name: POSA
commands.description: Searches the Alpha register for x (a character code or a string) and returns its position, or −1.

commands.name: PRA
commands.description: Prints the Alpha register.

commands.name: PRGM
commands.description: Turns program entry on or off.

commands.name: PRINT
commands.description: Opens the PRINT menu.

commands.name: PRLCD
commands.description: Prints what the display shows.

commands.name: PROB
commands.description: Opens the PROB menu: combinations, permutations, factorial, gamma, random numbers.

commands.name: PROFF
commands.description: Turns printing off (flags 21 and 55 cleared).

commands.name: PROMPT
commands.description: In a program: shows the Alpha register and stops.

commands.name: PRON
commands.description: Turns printing on (flags 21 and 55 set).

commands.name: PRP
commands.description: Prints a program, the current one if no label is given. Not programmable.

commands.name: PRSTK
commands.description: Prints X, Y, Z and T, the stack registers.

commands.name: PRUSR
commands.description: Prints the user variables and programs.

commands.name: PRV
commands.description: Prints a variable.

commands.name: PRX
commands.description: Prints the X-register.

commands.name: PRΣ
commands.description: Prints the summation registers.

commands.name: PSE
commands.description: In a program: pauses for about a second.

commands.name: PUTM
commands.description: Stores the matrix in x into the indexed matrix, from its current element.

commands.name: PWRF
commands.description: Power curve-fit model: y = b·x^m.

commands.name: QUIET
commands.description: Turns the beeper off or on (flag 26). Not programmable.

commands.name: RAD
commands.description: Radians angle mode.

commands.name: RAN
commands.description: A random number from 0 to just under 1.

commands.name: RCL
commands.description: Recalls a register or variable into x.

commands.name: RCL+
commands.description: Recalls a register or variable and adds it to x.

commands.name: RCL-
commands.description: Recalls a register or variable and subtracts it from x.

commands.name: RCL×
commands.description: Recalls a register or variable and multiplies x by it.

commands.name: RCL÷
commands.description: Recalls a register or variable and divides x by it.

commands.name: RCLEL
commands.description: Recalls the current element of the indexed matrix.

commands.name: RCLIJ
commands.description: Recalls I and J, the row and column pointers of the indexed matrix.

commands.name: RDX,
commands.description: Uses a comma as the decimal mark.

commands.name: RDX.
commands.description: Uses a point as the decimal mark.

commands.name: REALRES
commands.description: Real results only: a real argument that would give a complex result is an error.

commands.name: REAL?
commands.description: Tests whether x is a real number. A program runs its next line only if so.

commands.name: RECT
commands.description: Rectangular coordinate mode: complex numbers show as real and imaginary parts.

commands.name: RND
commands.description: Rounds x to the digits the display format shows.

commands.name: RNRM
commands.description: Row norm of x, a matrix: the largest sum of absolute values in one of its rows.

commands.name: ROTXY
commands.description: Rotates y, a 36-bit integer, by x bits: right for positive x, left for negative.

commands.name: RSUM
commands.description: Sums each row of x, a matrix, giving a column matrix of the sums.

commands.name: RTN
commands.description: Return: in a program it goes back to the line after the XEQ that called; from the keyboard it sets the program pointer to the program's top.

commands.name: R<>R
commands.description: Swaps rows y and x of the indexed matrix.

commands.name: R↑
commands.description: Rolls the stack up: x goes to y, y to z, z to t, t to x.
commands.stack: t z y x → z y x t

commands.name: R↓
commands.description: Rolls the stack down: t goes to z, z to y, y to x, x to t.
commands.stack: t z y x → x t z y

commands.name: R/S
commands.description: Runs the program from the current line, or stops a running one. In program entry it puts a STOP into the program.

commands.name: SCI
commands.description: Scientific notation with a number of digits after the point.

commands.name: SDEV
commands.description: The standard deviations of the x values and of the y values of the statistics data.

commands.name: SEED
commands.description: Starts the random number generator from x.

commands.name: SF
commands.description: Sets a flag.

commands.name: SHOW
commands.description: Shows x with all its digits, the whole Alpha register, or a whole program line, while the key is held.

commands.name: SIGN
commands.description: 1 for positive x and zero, −1 for negative x, 0 for anything not a number; for a complex x, the unit vector.

commands.name: SIMQ
commands.description: Sets up the matrix editor to solve simultaneous linear equations in a number of unknowns.

commands.name: SIN
commands.description: The sine of x, in the current angle mode.

commands.name: SINH
commands.description: The hyperbolic sine of x.

commands.name: SIZE
commands.description: Sets the number of numbered storage registers.

commands.name: SLOPE
commands.description: The slope of the current curve fit to the statistics data.

commands.name: SOLVE
commands.description: Solves the chosen program for an unknown variable.

commands.name: SOLVER
commands.description: Opens the SOLVER menu, for finding a value that makes a program's equation zero.

commands.name: SQRT
commands.description: The square root of x.

commands.name: SST
commands.description: Moves the program pointer forward one line, running that line outside program entry. With no menu shown, the ▼ key does it.

commands.name: STAT
commands.description: Opens the STAT menu: statistics and curve fitting.

commands.name: STO
commands.description: Stores a copy of x in a register or variable.

commands.name: STO+
commands.description: Adds x to a register or variable.

commands.name: STO-
commands.description: Subtracts x from a register or variable.

commands.name: STO×
commands.description: Multiplies a register or variable by x.

commands.name: STO÷
commands.description: Divides a register or variable by x.

commands.name: STOEL
commands.description: Stores x into the current element of the indexed matrix.

commands.name: STOIJ
commands.description: Moves the indexed matrix's pointers to row y and column x.

commands.name: STOP
commands.description: Stops a program. In program entry the R/S key puts it into the program.

commands.name: STR?
commands.description: Tests whether x holds an Alpha string. A program runs its next line only if so.

commands.name: SUM
commands.description: The sums of the x values and of the y values of the statistics data.

commands.name: TAN
commands.description: The tangent of x, in the current angle mode.

commands.name: TANH
commands.description: The hyperbolic tangent of x.

commands.name: TONE
commands.description: Plays one of ten tones, 0 to 9.

commands.name: TOP.FCN
commands.description: Opens the TOP.FCN menu: the functions of the top row of keys, for when another menu covers them.

commands.name: TRACE
commands.description: Trace print mode: the printer records the keys you press and the results.

commands.name: TRANS
commands.description: Transpose of x, a matrix.

commands.name: UVEC
commands.description: The matrix or complex number in x scaled to length 1, keeping its direction.

commands.name: VARMENU
commands.description: Builds a variable menu from the MVAR lines that follow a global label.

commands.name: VIEW
commands.description: Shows a register's or variable's contents.

commands.name: WMEAN
commands.description: The mean of the x values weighted by the y values.

commands.name: WRAP
commands.description: Wrap mode for the matrix editor: moving past the last element goes back to the first; the matrix does not grow.

commands.name: X<>
commands.description: Swaps x with a register or variable.

commands.name: X<>Y
commands.description: Swaps x and y.

commands.name: X<0?
commands.description: Tests whether x < 0. A program runs its next line only if so.

commands.name: X<Y?
commands.description: Tests whether x < y. A program runs its next line only if so.

commands.name: X≤0?
commands.description: Tests whether x ≤ 0. A program runs its next line only if so.

commands.name: X≤Y?
commands.description: Tests whether x ≤ y. A program runs its next line only if so.

commands.name: X=0?
commands.description: Tests whether x = 0. A program runs its next line only if so.

commands.name: X=Y?
commands.description: Tests whether x = y. A program runs its next line only if so.

commands.name: X≠0?
commands.description: Tests whether x ≠ 0. A program runs its next line only if so.

commands.name: X≠Y?
commands.description: Tests whether x ≠ y. A program runs its next line only if so.

commands.name: X>0?
commands.description: Tests whether x > 0. A program runs its next line only if so.

commands.name: X>Y?
commands.description: Tests whether x > y. A program runs its next line only if so.

commands.name: X≥0?
commands.description: Tests whether x ≥ 0. A program runs its next line only if so.

commands.name: X≥Y?
commands.description: Tests whether x ≥ y. A program runs its next line only if so.

commands.name: XEQ
commands.description: Runs a function or a program by its name or label.

commands.name: XOR
commands.description: The bitwise exclusive OR of y and x, as 36-bit integers.

commands.name: XTOA
commands.description: Appends the character with code x to the Alpha register; a string in x is appended whole.

commands.name: X↑2
commands.description: The square of x.

commands.name: YINT
commands.description: The y-intercept of the current curve fit to the statistics data.

commands.name: Y↑X
commands.description: y to the power x.

commands.name: ∫f(x)
commands.description: Opens the integration menu, for integrating a program's function.

commands.name: 1/X
commands.description: The reciprocal of x.

commands.name: 10↑X
commands.description: 10 to the power x.
Adds x to y.
Subtracts x from y.
Multiplies y by x.
Divides y by x.
Changes the sign of x, or of the exponent being typed.

commands.name: Σ+
commands.description: Adds the pair y, x to the statistics data in the summation registers; x shows the count.

commands.name: Σ-
commands.description: Takes the pair y, x out of the statistics data, to correct an entry.

commands.name: ΣREG
commands.description: Sets the first of the summation registers, which hold the statistics data.

commands.name: ΣREG?
commands.description: Which register the summation registers start at.

commands.name: →DEC
commands.description: Reads x as an octal number and gives its decimal value (for HP-41 programs; not the BASE menu).

commands.name: →DEG
commands.description: Converts an angle from radians to degrees.

commands.name: →HMS
commands.description: Converts decimal hours to hours-minutes-seconds form (H.MMSSss).

commands.name: →HR
commands.description: Converts hours-minutes-seconds (H.MMSSss) to decimal hours.

commands.name: →OCT
commands.description: Gives the octal digits of a decimal x, as a decimal-looking number (for HP-41 programs; not the BASE menu).

commands.name: →POL
commands.description: Converts x and y to polar form: the length r in x, the angle θ in y. A complex x is converted in place.

commands.name: →RAD
commands.description: Converts an angle from degrees to radians.

commands.name: →REC
commands.description: Converts polar form, the length r in x and the angle θ in y, to rectangular x and y. A complex x is converted in place.
Deletes the last character typed; with nothing being typed it clears x. In program entry it deletes the current line.
In the matrix editor: moves one element left.
In the matrix editor: moves one element up.
In the matrix editor: moves one element down.
In the matrix editor: moves one element right.
x percent of y; y stays.

commands.name: %CH
commands.description: The change from y to x as a percentage of y.
